t: You're standing at St Vedast Foster Lane, a church in Foster Lane in the City of London. It's dedicated to Saint Vedast, a French saint whose cult reached England through contacts with Augustinian clergy. Christopher Wren designed it, and he matters across the City: after the Great Fire of 1666 he was given the job of rebuilding fifty-two churches, with St Paul's Cathedral as his masterpiece. Also buried here is John Lonyson, a goldsmith who became Master of the Mint under Elizabeth the First.
